mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a single month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2%, this signals a strong demand environment coupled with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS < 2%
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong demand
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST increase and low FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a single month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, this signals inflationary pressure coupled with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 3%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of CPIAUCSL increase and high FEDFUNDS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in the same period, signals a robust supply-side expansion and a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases for 3 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
regime_hint: supply expansion with labor market tightening
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO increase and UNRATE decrease on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
